title: Reconstruction & Rebuild in Avondale, AZ | Gold Water Fire | Phoenix, AZ
description: Reconstruction and rebuild for Avondale homes after water or fire damage. Gold Water Fire, Chandler based, serving the Phoenix metro. Call (480) 999-3339.
intro: The demolition is done and the drying equipment is gone, and what is left is a room with the drywall cut off at two feet, bare studs, and a floor that stops halfway across. You have been living around it. Maybe you have been the one making the calls, taking the photos the adjuster asked for, keeping a folder on the kitchen counter, telling your kids to walk around the plastic sheeting. That part is exhausting in a way that is hard to explain to anyone who has not done it, because the emergency is over but the house still is not a house.

sections.heading: Putting an Avondale house back together after mitigation
sections.body: Reconstruction is the second half of a damage claim and it works differently from the first half. Mitigation is about stopping loss: extraction, containment, drying, removing unsalvageable material. Reconstruction is about restoring the structure to pre-loss condition, which means framing repairs, insulation, drywall hang and finish, texture match, paint, trim, cabinetry, countertops, flooring, and the finish carpentry that makes a repair stop looking like a repair. In Arizona, matching an orange peel or knockdown texture on a patched wall is its own skill, and a bad match is the thing homeowners notice every day for years. Where the work touches structure, gas, or electrical, permitting through the City of Avondale comes into it, and the scope has to be written so the insurance carrier and the building department are looking at the same job.

cards.heading: Scope and estimate
cards.body: Line by line documentation of what has to be rebuilt, written in the format carriers work from, so the conversation is about the house rather than about paperwork.

cards.heading: Structure and systems
cards.body: Framing, subfloor, insulation, and coordination of the electrical, plumbing, and HVAC work that has to happen before anything gets closed up.

cards.heading: Finishes
cards.body: Drywall and texture, paint, baseboard and casing, doors, flooring, cabinets and counters, with attention to matching what is already in the rest of the home.

cards.heading: Final walkthrough
cards.body: A punch list you help write, so the job ends when the house is right, not when the schedule says it should be.

sections.heading: The housing stock and weather here shape the repair
sections.body:
Avondale grew fast. A large share of the city's homes went up during the late 1990s and 2000s boom along the Estrella Parkway and Dysart corridors, in subdivisions like Garden Lakes, Rancho Santa Fe, Coldwater Springs, and the newer stretches south of the river toward Estrella. That era of West Valley production building has consistent traits that matter when you rebuild: slab on grade with no crawlspace, so a supply line failure spreads laterally through carpet pad and under baseboard instead of draining away; engineered wood or laminate flooring that swells and delaminates rather than dries; PEX or copper manifolds in walls; second floor laundry rooms above a great room in the two story plans, which turns a burst washer hose into a ceiling replacement; and stucco over foam on the exterior, where damage repair has to be sealed properly or it will fail again. A lot of these homes are now hitting the age where original water heaters, angle stops, and washing machine hoses give out.

The seasonal pattern here is its own thing. Monsoon storms roll into the West Valley off the desert with blowing dust ahead of the rain, and the microburst winds that come with them lift tile and lift or peel roof edges, so the leak often shows up days later at an interior ceiling. Avondale also sits along the Gila and Agua Fria confluence, and low lying areas near the riverbeds and the older drainage channels take on water when a storm dumps hard and fast. Then in January and February the reverse problem: a cold snap on an unprotected hose bib or an exposed line in an uninsulated garage wall. If your damage came from any of those, the rebuild has to fix the cause, not just the drywall, or you will be doing it again.

sections.heading: Who does the work and how the handoff goes
sections.body: Gold Water Fire is a licensed Arizona contractor, AZ ROC #264344 · KB-2, based at 221 E Willis Rd Ste 8 in Chandler and working across the Phoenix metro, from NW Peoria to SE Avondale, SW San Tan Valley, NW Apache Junction, and outlying areas beyond that. The company was founded by Jim Bennett and Jake Taylor. Reconstruction is led by Brandon Gurr, our Construction Manager, who came to us from running Gurr Brothers Construction, and Johnny leads the reconstruction crews on site. Kristine handles the office and Brooke handles water and mitigation scheduling, so when you call there is a person who knows your job rather than a queue. The reason it helps to have one company carry both halves is simple. When the crew that dried your house is on the same team as the crew that rebuilds it, nobody has to re-discover what was behind the wall, and no one gets to point at the other guy when something in the scope is missing. If you are earlier in this than you think, the water damage restoration and fire damage restoration pages cover what happens before the rebuild starts. More on how reconstruction runs is on the reconstruction and rebuild page, and you can read about the people doing it on the about page.

faqs.q: Can you rebuild if another company did the water or fire mitigation?
faqs.a: Yes. We regularly pick up jobs where the drying or cleanup was handled by someone else. We will want to see the moisture readings and the demolition photos if you have them, along with the mitigation invoice, so the rebuild scope lines up with what was already removed and what the carrier has already paid for.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rebuild my Avondale home after damage?
faqs.a: It depends on the scope. Like most Arizona municipalities, the City of Avondale generally requires permits for structural framing changes and for electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work, while cosmetic replacement of drywall, paint, and flooring often does not. We identify what your specific job needs and pull what is required as part of the scope rather than leaving it to you.

faqs.q: Will my new drywall texture and paint match the rest of the house?
faqs.a: Matching is a real part of the work. Knockdown and orange peel textures vary by original applicator, and Arizona sun fades paint over time, so an exact-formula color match on a patched wall can still read differently than the adjacent wall. Where that is the case, we will tell you before we start and discuss wrapping the repair to a natural break line, like a corner or ceiling line, so the finished room reads as one room.

faqs.q: How do you handle the insurance side of a reconstruction claim?
faqs.a: We write the rebuild scope in line item detail and document it with photos so your adjuster can review the same information we are working from. Coverage decisions belong to your carrier, but a clearly written and well documented scope removes most of the back and forth, and we will talk directly with your adjuster so you are not the one relaying messages.

cta.heading: You do not have to project manage this
cta.body: If your Avondale home is sitting half torn out and you are tired of being the one holding it all together, call Gold Water Fire at (480) 999-3339 or email Help@goldwaterfire.com. Tell us what happened and what has already been done, and we will walk the house with you and put together the scope to finish it.
